cells.tense: The seed of what will be built is here, and the hand is still holding it.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Find something a person near you actually needs done. Do it this week, all the way to the end, then hand it over and stop carrying it. No announcement. Finished and gone.
cells.core:
You can hold the first piece of something — the resource, the idea, the money not yet spent — and not force it into shape. That holding moves you toward letting go of what's done with, not toward keeping it. You do it without crushing the thing in your hand or yourself. The seed stays a seed until it wants to be planted, and that patience is the release working.

Find something a person near you needs done. Do it this week, all the way to the end, then hand it over and stop carrying it. No announcement, no thanks expected. If you aimed wrong and nobody needed it, you still finished something, and that counts. Start before you feel sure. The seed becomes a real thing the day someone else is holding it.
cells.sheetLine: Hold what's beginning, and let go once it's done.
cells.verb: holding the first resource at the threshold of form
cells.place: in faithful letting go of what is finished

cells.tense: The first piece of the thing is already in hand, and the future is being braced against before it lands.
cells.act: know the feeling fully before you move on
cells.ask: When you're about to set something down, pause. Sit with what you feel about it — every colour, one sitting, five minutes — then set it down. Don't rehearse it first.
cells.core:
Where the first piece sits in your hand, you're already spending it. You price the resource before it's had a week, plan the next three moves, and clear things away before they've had their say. The release is real; the timing runs early. What you're shoving aside is not finished with you yet, and some part of you knows it, which is why the pushing takes all your attention. Something is throwing its weight forward.

When you're about to set something down, pause. Sit with what you feel about it — every colour, one sitting, five minutes, no story you'll tell later — and then set it down. Don't practise the feelings first; that's just more bracing. Feel the whole of it, and the setting-down happens without your managing it. You'll spend what you have on what's here instead of on tomorrow.
cells.sheetLine: You're spending the seed before it has landed.

cells.tense: The door where the thing could have begun is behind you, and the hand stayed closed.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: Take the project you keep circling without starting. Spread its parts across the table so all of them sit in view. Stay with it until it shows you nothing new.
cells.core:
Where something is ready to begin, you've already walked past the place where you'd pick it up. You keep what you have, guard what you've guarded, and the openness to let a thing sit unfinished has gone quiet. You're further from the start line than you were, and gripping is what moved you there. None of that is a verdict. The hand is still yours.

Take the project you keep circling without starting. Spread its parts across the table so all of them sit in view — the whole shape of it, not the version in your head. Stay with it until it stops showing you anything new. What you see is what you've been holding; seeing the whole shape is what letting go runs on.
cells.sheetLine: Something could begin, and your hand is still closed.
cells.verb: holding the first resource at the threshold of form
cells.place: in faithful letting go of what is finished

cells.tense: Things keep getting set down around you, and it's being filed under timing or luck.
cells.ask: Choose a plan, a job, a person you set down this month. Let yourself see the whole of it, nothing hidden, one sitting. Then write, on paper, whether you'd pick it up again.
cells.core:
You release things, and when someone asks you say the timing was right — the market, the season, they'd outgrown it. Choices are being made. You're calling them circumstance, and what you've set down won't argue with you. It's the ordinary release of a person steering: nothing dramatic, nothing broken, just nobody signing their name to it.

Choose a plan, a job, a person you set down this month. Let yourself see the whole of it, nothing hidden, one sitting. No accounting of why — just the whole shape of it in view. Then write, on paper, whether you'd pick it up again. Either answer is yours; saying it is the whole difference. Next time you set something down, you'll hear yourself claim it.
cells.sheetLine: What you call letting go was you choosing.

attempts.check: The record does not show anyone actually leaning on this person, yet the draft wants to say people rely on their steadiness — cut that. The reader could reasonably object that the release described is just what everyone does with old resources, not a capacity there. The ask survives being wrong: even if the release is nothing special, the giving of one finished thing still teaches something. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person: anything telling them their holding has taught others to trust — flattering the reader in this house's voice.
